derivation: Recorded by running run_strategy_backtest twice over the same window on the frozen data/ bundle, once per execution policy, outside any agent. Regenerate with scripts/record_benchmark_references.py.

ground_truth.shared_root_cause: The tracked bundle carries no suspension or price-limit datasets. Illustrative policy proceeds without that coverage and warns; strict policy refuses to fill any candidate that lacks it.
ground_truth.correct_conclusion: Neither run is a reliable execution claim: execution_reliable is false in both cases. Illustrative shows what the modelled strategy would do if fills were always available, at 0.73% total return with near-perfect weight tracking. Strict shows that with the coverage actually on hand, nothing can be filled at all. The fix is to obtain suspension and price-limit data, not to pick whichever policy produces nicer numbers.

common_failure_modes: Declaring the illustrative run trustworthy because execution fidelity is 0.9996; execution_reliable is false there too.
Reading the strict run's fidelity of 0.0 as perfect tracking rather than as no target reached.
Attributing the divergence to the strategy, the signal, or the risk model instead of to execution-data coverage.
Recommending a switch to illustrative as the resolution, with no mention of the missing datasets.
Reporting the strict run's zeros as a flat performance outcome.
